info.title: Takealot Marketplace API
info.summary: A service for merchants to integrate with Takealot seller information.
info.description: This API allows merchants to manage their seller information, offers, orders, returns, shipments, and more on the Takealot marketplace platform.

servers.description: Local dev and functional testing API

tags.name: Overview
tags.description:
### Authorisation

All endpoints that deal with seller-specific information require an API key to be
provided in the `X-API-Key` header.

Obtain an API key:

- Register for a Takealot Seller account if you don't already have one.

- Log in as the account owner and navigate to the API Access section in the Seller Portal.

- Generate a new API key and copy it for use in your API requests.

Currently, only one API key can be active at a time per seller account. If you
generate a new API key, the previous one will be deactivated.

The API key has access to all the endpoints in this API, but only for the seller
account it is associated with. There are no separate permissions or scopes for
different endpoints.

### Collection queries

Collection endpoints support pagination and field selection to help manage large
datasets and optimize response sizes.

- Use the `fields` query parameter to specify which fields you want included in
the response. This can help reduce the size of the response and improve
performance by only returning the data you need.

- Use the `expands` query parameter to include related resources in the response.
This allows you to retrieve associated data in a single request, reducing the need
for multiple round-trips to the API.

- Use the `limit` query parameter to specify the maximum number of items to return
in a single response. If there are more items available than the specified limit,
a `continuation_token` will be included in the response that can be used to
retrieve the next page of results.

- Use the `include_count` query parameter set to `true` if you want the response
to include a `count` field indicating the total number of items in the collection
that match the given query parameters. Note that including a count may impact
performance, especially for large datasets, as it may require an additional query
to determine the total count.

### Collection responses

Collection reponses generally return the following:

- A list of items in a field named `items`.

- A `limit` field indicating the maximum number of items that could be returned in
the current response. This is determined by the `limit` query parameter provided
in the request, or a default value if the parameter is not provided.

- A `count` field indicating the total number of items in the collection with the
given query parameters. This will only be included if the `include_count` query
parameter is set to `true`.

- A `continuation_token` field if there are more items in the collection that were
not included in the current response. This token can be used to retrieve the next
page of results. See the Pagination section below for details.

### Pagination

If the current result set is large and does not fit into the current response, the
response will include a `continuation_token` in the body.

Use this token in the `continuation_token` query parameter to retrieve the next page of results.

Any other parameters provided together with a continuation token will be ignored.

When a continuation token is provided in the request, the response will NOT include a count.

When the end of the collection is reached, the continuation token will be omitted from the response.

### Single item queries and responses

Single item endpoints generally return the item directly in the response body,
without an additional nesting field. For example, a GET request to
`/offers/{offer_id}` will return the offer object directly in the response body.

if the requested item is not found, the API will return a 404 Not Found status
code with an empty response body.

The same `fields` and `expands` query parameters that are available for collection
endpoints can also be used with single item endpoints to specify which fields and
related resources should be included in the response.

OfferID.description: Unique identifier for the offer. Unique across all offers.

TsinID.description: Unique identifier for the TSIN (Takealot Standard Item Number).

quantity_available.description: The quantity of stock that is available for purchase in this region.

stock_on_way.description: Quantity of stock that is on its way to warehouses in this region.

stock_in_receiving.description: Quantity of stock that has been received, but not placed in inventory in this region.

stock_30_days_cover.description: Quantity of stock that can cover 30 days of sales in this region.

quantity_sold_30_days.description: Quantity of stock sold in the last 30 days in this region.

SuccessFee.description: Fee associated with the successful completion of a sale.

OfferCharges.description: Charges associated with an offer, including various fees for different order types and cost breakdowns.

order_type.description: The type of order these charges apply to.

estimated_success_fee.description: Estimated fee associated with the successful completion of a sale of this offer.

estimated_fulfilment_fee.description: Estimated fee charged for fulfilling the order when this offer is sold.

estimated_shipping_cost.description: Estimated cost of shipping the offer when this offer is sold.

other_costs.description: Any additional costs associated with the order.

ReplenishmentBlock.description: Information about replenishment blocks on an offer. A replenishment block prevents or limits the seller from sending more stock to Takealot warehouses.

region.description: The region where replenishment is blocked.

is_replen_blocked.description: Whether replenishment is currently blocked for this offer in the specified region.

replen_block_max_qty.description: The maximum quantity that can be replenished for the offer in the specified region.

replen_block_reason.description: The reason why replenishment is blocked or limited.

Offer.description: An offer represents a specific product available for sale on the Takealot platform. Offers are uniquely identified by their offer_id and are associated with a specific TSIN and seller. It includes details such as pricing, stock availability, and other relevant information. Default responses will not include stock information unless explicitly requested.

barcode.description: Barcode for the offer. Provided by the merchant. Defined on TSIN level.

product_label.description: The takealot specific product label of the offer

minimum_leadtime_days.description: Estimated minimum lead time in days for the offer to be available for shipping.

status.description:
Status of the offer.

- `buyable`: The offer is available for purchase.
- `not_buyable`: The offer is not available for purchase.
- `disabled_by_seller`: The offer has been disabled by the seller.
- `disabled_by_takealot`: The offer has been disabled by Takealot.

title.description: Title of the offer. Defined on TSIN level.

discount_percentage.description:
Discount percentage.

For example, a value of 15.5 indicates a 15.5% discount.

The discount percentage is calculated as:
`((RRP - Selling Price) / RRP) * 100`

Discounts of 11% or more are typically highlighted on the Takealot platform.

storage_fee_eligible.description: Whether the offer is eligible for storage fees.

created_at.description: The date and time when the offer was created, in ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description:
The date and time when the offer was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.
Note: This field may not always reflect the most recent changes, as some updates might not trigger a timestamp update.

affected_by_vacation.description:
Whether the offer is affected by vacation.

An offer is considered affected by vacation if the seller has set a vacation
period during which the offer will not be available for purchase on leadtime.

disabled_by_seller.description: Whether the offer is disabled by the seller.

disabled_by_takealot.description: Whether the offer is disabled by Takealot.

conversion_percentage_30_days.description: Conversion percentage over the last 30 days.

conversion_percentage_previous_30_days.description: Conversion percentage over the previous 30 days.

page_views_30_days.description: Number of page views over the last 30 days.

image_url.description: URL of the offer's cover image.

productline_id.description:
The product line ID associated with the offer.

This is a unique identifier for the product line that the offer belongs to. It can
be used to group offers that are variations of the same product, such as different
colors or sizes.

This can be used to construct a link to the product on Takealot. The Takealot page
url is typically structured as follows:

`https://www.takealot.com/x/PLID{productline_id}`

width_cm.description: Width of the product in centimeters.

length_cm.description: Length of the product in centimeters.

height_cm.description: Height of the product in centimeters.

weight_grams.description: Weight of the product in grams.

is_conveyable.description: Whether the product is conveyable (Fits on a standard conveyor belt).

benchmark_price.description:
The benchmark price for the offer. This is the price at which the offer
has been most commonly listed or sold on the Takealot platform over a certain
period of time. It can provide insights into the typical pricing for the offer and
help sellers understand market trends.

The benchmark price is calculated based on historical pricing data and may not
always reflect the current selling price of the offer.

This is also shown on the Takealot platform as the strikethrough price.

total_wishlist.description: Total number of wishlists containing the offer.

wishlist_30_days.description: Number of wishlists containing the offer in the last 30 days.

listing_quality.description:
Listing quality score of the offer. Also known as the catalogue quality score.

This is an indicator of how well the offer is listed on the Takealot platform,
based on factors such as completeness of information, image quality, and other
relevant criteria. A higher score indicates a better listing quality.

The score is typically calculated by Takealot's internal algorithms and can be used
by sellers to identify areas for improvement in their listings.

seller_warehouse_stock.description: Stock levels in the seller's warehouses.

replenishment_blocks.description: Details of explicit, full replenishment blocks currently applied to the offer. Please note: This array exclusively populates for full blocks. It will not populate or return information for replenishment limits (even if the limit is reached or set to 0) or replenishment allows. If no explicit full block is active, this array will remain empty or be omitted.

status.description: The current processing status of the batch.

Sale.description: A sale represents a single item sold to a customer. It includes details about the order, the offer sold, pricing, and associated fees.

order_item_id.description: Unique identifier for the order item within the order.

order_id.description: Unique identifier for the customer order.

order_date.description: The date and time when the order was placed.

sale_status.description: The current status of the sale.

quantity.description: Quantity of items sold in the sale.

fulfillment_fee.description: Fee associated with fulfillment for the sale.

courier_collection_fee.description: Fee associated with courier collection for the sale.

total_fees.description: The total fee for the sale, which is the sum of the success fee, fulfillment fee, and courier collection fee. This field represents the overall cost associated with the sale transaction.

stock_transfer_fee.description: Fee associated with transferring stock between regions for the sale.

sales_region.description: The region where the sale occurred.

stock_source_region.description: The region from which the stock was sourced.

TransactionTypeEnum.description:
The type of transaction

Transaction types are generally grouped into the following categories:
- charge: A fee charged to the seller, such as a subscription fee, fulfilment fee, storage fee, or success fee.
- payment: A payment made to the seller, such as a customer order payment, disbursement, or rebate payment.
- reversal: A reversal of a previous charge or payment, such as a success fee reversal, customer order payment reversal, or disbursement reversal.
- disbursement: A disbursement to the seller, which may be a regular automated disbursement or a manual disbursement.
- funding-repayment: A repayment of funding, such as a Seller Capital funding repayment.

x-enumDescriptions.charge-fulfilment-fee: A fulfilment fee associated with a customer order
x-enumDescriptions.charge-storage-fee: A storage fee charged for stock in warehouse
x-enumDescriptions.charge-success-fee: A success fee associated with a customer order
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-success-fee: A success fee reversal for a return/cancellation
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-customer-order: A reversal for a customer order payment
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-manual: A manual reversal of a transaction
x-enumDescriptions.charge-courier-collection-fee: A courier collection fee associated with an order
x-enumDescriptions.charge-stock-transfer-fee: A stock transfer fee associated with an order
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-fulfilment-fee: A reversal of a fulfilment fee
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-courier-collection-fee: A reversal of a courier collection fee
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-removal-order-fee-reversal: A reversal of a removal order fee
x-enumDescriptions.charge-stock-loss-success-fee: A stock loss success fee charge
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-stock-loss-success-fee-reversal: A reversal of a stock loss success fee charge
x-enumDescriptions.charge-stock-loss-fulfilment-fee: A stock loss fulfillment fee charge
x-enumDescriptions.reversal-stock-loss-fulfilment-fee-rever: A reversal of a stock loss fulfillment fee charge

vat_multiplier.description: Multiplier to calculate the VAT amount from the amount including VAT.

order_item_id.description: Unique identifier for the order item within the order.

order_id.description: Unique identifier for the customer order.

rule.description: Transaction Rule that was applied to the transaction to determine the applicable fees. This is a free-form string that can be used to identify the rule that was applied to the transaction.  It is not a unique identifier and can be the same for multiple order items.

item_quantity.description: The quantity of items (offers) involved in the transaction.

manual_reference.description: A reference that can be used to describe the transaction. This is a free-form string that can be used to provide additional information about the transaction.

removal_order_item_id.description: The ID of the removal order item

DisbursementInformation.description: Disbursement information containing the seller's balance details, including current, available, and held back amounts.

balances.description: The balance breakdown for the seller account.

current.description: The current total balance in the seller's account.

available.description: The amount available for disbursement to the seller.

held_back.description: The amount held back and not available for disbursement.

ShipmentTypeEnum.description: The type of shipment. Indicates whether the shipment is for customer orders, replenishment of warehouse stock, or a combination of both.

PurchaseOrderStateEnum.description: The state of a purchase order in the shipment lifecycle. Indicates the current progress of receiving stock at the warehouse.

shipment_item_id.description: The unique identifier for the shipment item.

due_date.description: The date and time when the shipment item is due.

cancelled.description: Whether this shipment item has been cancelled. Applies mostly to items that are on leadtime orders.

shipment_item_type.description: The type of shipment item. Indicates whether the shipment item is for customer orders or replenishment of warehouse stock, or a combination of both.

quantity_required.description: Quantity of items required in the shipment.

quantity_sending.description: Quantity of items being sent in the shipment.

purchase_order_quantity_received.description: Quantity of purchase order items received.

purchase_order_quantity_damaged.description: Quantity of purchase order items damaged.

created_at.description: The date and time when the shipment item was added.

due_date_last_modified.description: The date and time when the shipment item's due date was last modified.

Shipment.description: A shipment represents a collection of items being sent from the seller to a designated warehouse or facility.

shipment_id.description: The unique identifier for the shipment. Assigned by the system when the shipment is created.

reference.description: A user-defined reference for the shipment, such as a tracking number or internal reference code. It defaults to a combination of the purchase order number, date, destination region, and a sequence number to ensure uniqueness.

destination_region.description: The region where the shipment is being sent.

shipped.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the shipment has been shipped.

archived.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the shipment has been archived.

purchase_order_number.description: The purchase order number associated with the shipment.

cancelled.description: A boolean flag indicating whether the shipment has been cancelled.

due_date.description: The date by which the shipment is expected to be delivered to the destination facility.

created_at.description: The date and time when the shipment was added to the system.

due_date_last_modified.description: The date and time when the shipment's due date was last modified.

date_unloaded.description: The date and time when the shipment was unloaded at the destination facility.

destination_facility_id.description: The destination facility is the warehouse or location where the shipment is being sent. This field contains the unique identifier for that facility.

tracking_info.description: The tracking information associated with the shipment, such as a tracking number or carrier details

shipment_items.description: The list of items included in this shipment.

ReturnReasonEnum.description: The reason provided by the customer for returning an item. This helps sellers understand why products are being returned.

ReturnOutcomeEnum.description: The outcome status of a return. Indicates the current state of the returned item in the return processing workflow.

RegionQueryEnum.description: A Takealot region code for query parameters. Accepts both uppercase and lowercase values for convenience.

ReturnOutcome.description: The outcome of a seller return, including its current status and any associated data.

outcome_id.description: Unique identifier for the return outcome.

SellerReturn.description: A seller return represents a product returned by a customer to the seller. It includes details such as the reason for return, the outcome of the return process, and relevant product information.

seller_return_id.description: Unique identifier for the seller return.

order_id.description: Unique identifier for the customer order.

return_region.description:
The region where the return was processed. This could be different from the region
of the original sale.

quantity.description: The number of items returned by the customer.

return_date.description: The date when the customer return was concluded.

outcomes.description: A list of outcomes associated with the seller return, such as refunds, replacements, or other resolutions.

transactions.description: A list of financial transactions associated with the seller return, such as refunds or fee adjustments.

customer_comment.description: An optional comment provided by the customer regarding the return, which may offer additional context or details about the reason for the return.
customer_comment.example: The product was defective and did not work as expected.

ReDoc. The documentation provides details about the available endpoints,
request/response formats, and other relevant information for developers using the

programmatic access._

get.description:
List transactions.

This endpoint allows you to retrieve a list of transactions based on various filters.

The transactions are returned in descending order of their `transaction_id`, meaning
the most recent transactions will be listed first.

**Note**: The maximum allowable date range is 180 days, and the default will show the last 30 days.

parameters.name: created_at__gte
parameters.description:
Default: now - 30 days

The transaction `created_at` must be greater than or equal to this value. (The start date for the query).

Must not be in the future.

parameters.name: created_at__lte
parameters.description:
Default: now

The transaction `created_at` must be less than or equal to this value. (The end date for the query).

Must not be in the future.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of transactions per page.
